4. Economic Effects of the Proposed Improvement.
General Mitchell Field, a major traffic generator, represents a substantial contribution to the Milwaukee Metropolitan economy.

A prosperous community must have a viable airport that is easily accessible. An airport fraeway facility directly connecting General Mitchell Field with the existing Interstate and Milwaukee County Freeway systems will greatly increase the accessibility of the airport. It is compatible with long range planning for the airport. The facility is consistent with regional and local goals and objectives and is in the public interest.
The economic importance of General Mitchell Field can be measured in terms of taxes, income, services, employment, and business activity. It is also an attraction for sightseers and tourists.

Additional benefits derived from General Mitchell Field are the businesses established in the vicinity of the airport. These include restaurants, motels, and taxicab and limousine service companies. Construction expenditures for improving airport facilities can also be included.

Without the desire for air travel, there would be no need for an airport. However, according to studies by Milwaukee County's airport facility consultants, the growth of air travel and the need for upgrading Mitchell Field airport facilities is foreseen throughout the next two decades with flight activity for 1990 projected to triple that of 1972. It is expected that substantial expenditures by Milwaukee County will be required to improve or expand the existing facilities of General Mitchell Field.
